title: A later conditional CSS rule can erase the visual state it only intended to restyle
trigger: A base state rule paints a visual indicator, but a later :not(:hover)/state-specific rule writes the same property for a subset of states.
principle: Check the cascade per visual property, not only whether the base rule exists. If a state indicator must remain visible, conditional restyling rules must not overwrite that property unless the hiding behavior is part of the contract; regression tests should assert computed style for every state and surface.

cases.context: Token status CSS painted a semantic inset underline for every status, then a later known/ignore :not(:hover) rule replaced box-shadow with the generic shadow. Unknown/tracking showed underlines, while known/ignore looked unstyled until hover.
